title: SGD Jittering: A Training Strategy for Robust and Accurate Model-Based Architectures
summary: Core risk derivations omit noise-dependent covariances; a finite-unrolling scalar example reverses both comparisons. A separate exact recurrence violates Corollary6.2 by factor16.
limitations: Finite two-step risk comparison applies to finite-unrolling interpretation used in proof, not exact argmin interpretation.
No author-code execution, data download, imaging or attack reproduction.
Cited convergence theorem not separately retrieved; finding is direct counterexample to the paper's corollary.
No global later-version or erratum search.
Separate OpenReview supplement presence unresolved after source-preparation HTTP403.

problems.source_claim: Theorems7.4-7.5 guarantee lower generalization and robustness risks than optimal MSE training.
problems.location: pp5-6; AppendixC p15 final display and p16 conclusion; AppendixD p16 risk expansion
assumptions: Two-step architecture eta1/2, initial y; w0=0
Independent Gaussian observation, jittering and evaluation noises; all scales arbitrarily small
Parameter a in [1,3/2]; both optima exist uniquely
Finite-K interpretation explicitly separated from exact argmin
problems.check: AppendixC omits -2E[BN]=-a*s^2/8. AppendixD omits 2E[eB]=-2eta*a*variance(e). Exact K2 training objective has a_sgd=1.3894887313 vs a_mse1.5; both inference risks larger at jittered optimum.
problems.result: Both displayed identities false; finite-unrolling universal comparisons false.
problems.counterevidence: Exact argmin differs from finite architecture. AppendixD's closing equal-clean-risk qualification is not satisfied by comparison but does not fix covariance identities. Benchmarks can improve.
problems.core_dependency: Simultaneous theoretical generalization and robustness improvement is the main stated contribution.
problems.impact: Major for invalid central proof; no empirical result asserted false.

correction.reason: Covariance terms identified; no repaired theorem certified.
